recipes.name: Roasted Apples and Brussels Sprouts
ingredients_raw: 2 apples - peeled, cored, and cut into 3/4-inch chunks
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, or as needed
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).

Arrange frozen Brussels sprouts in a single layer on a rimmed baking sheet; sprinkle apple and onion pieces evenly around the baking sheet. Drizzle the sprouts, apples, and onions with olive oil; sprinkle with salt, black pepper, and garlic powder. Toss the mixture gently to coat.
Roast in the preheated oven until sprouts are hot and fragrant, about 20 minutes. Sprinkle with lemon zest, and squeeze juice from zested lemon over the sprouts to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Roasted Apples and Brussels Sprouts
raw_recipe.description: Frozen Brussels sprouts get an upgrade in flavor when roasted with apple and sweet onion chunks and drizzled with lemon. You don't even have to thaw the sprouts--just pour them frozen from the bag onto the baking sheet, season, and roast.

review.reviewBody:
I rarely assign 5 stars, because it means there is zero room for improvement. I have given this recipe one of my coveted 5-star ratings, as I truly don't see any way to make it better.

Starting with the frozen Brussels sprouts. I urge you not to think you will improve this recipe by using fresh. Unless you are pulling them from your own garden, Brussels sprouts are never truly fresh, and they rapidly deteriorate once harvested. If you MUST use fresh, be sure to at least use the ones that come still attached to the stalk. The reason they sell them that way is because of the rapid deterioration these vegetable experience once harvested. This is also why so many people think they don't like Brussels sprouts! 

The mixture of apples and onions into this recipe is perfect, and the lemon adds a nice tang.

As the original recipe notes in the footnotes, you can adjust roasting time for desired doneness. I find that 40 minutes produces a better result, turning the vegetables every 10-15 minutes for even browning. You want them slightly darkened and caramelized. I am experimenting with using the convection feature of our oven to see if I can achieve this effect quicker. Best to use non-stick foil to line your roasting pan to prevent sticking.

This is a good, solid dish. The apples and the onions play off of each other well, and the brussels sprouts come out nicely seared, giving them the best possible flavor. I do have a few notes to take this from a 4 to a 5, though:

First, tossing the sprouts, apples, and onions in the oil instead of drizzling will help coat them completely and get a better bake on them. 

Second, pecans. a cup of untoasted pecans added before baking will make this dish really pop. I added mine after trying the dish, and it definitely enhanced the flavor.

Delicious! 
Like several others. I added balsamic vinegar to the oil, added the apples after 15 min and baked for a total of 30. Was a big hit and will definitely make again!

Love this recipe; a keeper. However, old age perhaps laziness(?), caused me to make some changes (...just because, but, not necessary). 1) used fresh Brussels Sprouts; cut off ends & cut in half (like them really roasted) 2) left on apple skins (red, fuji); (liked color added; heck, was just easier!) 3) added lots more olive oil (the coated seasonings along w/the after-baked spritzed lemon juice make this great!) (*left off the zest, just easier-but for company-may add) 4) to salt & pepper, added pinch(es) of cayenne pepper 5) Hand-mixed to coat all really well (may do in a bowl first next time; but probably not) 6) Baked on a non-stick cookie sheet (may try baking paper; but probably not; the (new!) non-stick cookie sheet was best--easy cleanup & let the oil & spices bead up, absorb into veggies) 7) ...thought about adding bacon as a topping (maybe next time; too much trouble this time). Thought about adding fresh garlic (definitely next time). Cynthia L

Tasty and easy! I took some recomendations from others and I started on the stove with the onions and brussels sprouts, cooked until caramelized. Added apples and dried cranberries, cooked on stovetop for a while then added salt and pepper. Transfered onto parchment paper lined cookie sheet and cooked for 25 mins....will add lemon juice and zest before serving!

Did as others and started with olive oil, thawed brussel sprouts chopped in half, fresh garlic and 1 purple onion cooked in a skillet until caramelized. Transferred to a baking sheet, added the apples, another drizzle of oil and cooked on 250 while I made a quick run to the store. Toasted almond slivers in the seasoned skillet and added these at the end after a drizzle of lemon juice. Very very good. Teenager and 3 kids under 10 ate these up.

Excellent, and my new favourite Brussel sprout. Recipe! I used 3 smashed garlic cloves instead of the powder. Also tossed everything together in a bowl with the oil to coat evenly. Added some sea salt before serving along with the lemon zest and juice.. Which was most delish. Next time I will be roasting my zested lemon along with the Brussels to get the lemon juice nice a sweet. Used fresh Brussels halved..took 35 minutes to cook.

I used fresh brussel sprouts. I blanched them for 2 minutes then into an icewater bath and drain. This helps to keep the green color. This will be my go to recipe for brussel sprouts. It was delicious. The apples provide just a little sweetness and the lemon and zest give it a fresh punch.

I used fresh Brussels sprouts. Proportions for my taste would be a third of each : 1/3 sprouts, 1/3 onions, 1/3 apples. I sliced them all thinly as I was in a rush : this way cooking only takes 10 mn in a frying pan. The lemon does bring a plus. Great with chunks of bacon or ham on the top.

I made this last night with about double the quantity of fresh Brussels sprouts, one good sized Fuji apple, and about 3/4 of an average sized Vidalia onion (what I had in the house). The ratio was fine, the flavors were good. I roasted until the sprouts were just getting crispy on the top, and the apple was getting soft, stirring it all around on the baking sheet every 15 minutes or so. Everyone enjoyed it, and it was easy. I will make it again.

This was even better the second day! I live alone, so I adjusted the recipe for 4 servings and wrapped the leftovers in aluminum foil and warmed them in a 350 degree oven for about 30 minutes the next day. Oh-la-la! The Brussels sprouts were so tender, and the apples' deliciousness blended in even more lusciously . Oh yes, I substituted white wine for the lemon - I always substitute white wine for lemon - it's an idiosyncrasy of mine...
Had flavor of just off the grill and it's so healthy and low in calories

Roasted brussels sprouts, apples, and onion is a good flavor trio. I used fresh brussels sprouts rather than frozen and left them whole, except for a couple large ones which I halved. Next time I make this I’ll cut all the brussels sprouts in half to hopefully shorten the cooking time to be more in sync with the apples and onions. It took 38 minutes at 425ºF for the whole sprouts to cook through, and when the cooked onions and apples were starting to get very brown, I loosely covered the baking sheet with foil. Also, I will not peel the apples. I think this dish would benefit from a pop of color from red apple skin to give it some eye appeal. Also, peeled, the apples look like potatoes, although once you bite into one, you get that layer of sweetness. But bottom line, this is a delicious side dish, just needs a few tweaks for me.
So simple and Delicious
I ended up picking out the brussel sprouts by themselves so it wouldn't be a complete waste. It just was not good.
Excellent! I added a half teaspoon of kosher salt and some pecans. Love the freshness of the lemon!
Made it again and again ! delicious
Literally, this is one of my favorite recipes on this site. I added apples and well, BACON! It tastes like Fall Yall (poor bacon., now I feel guilty, but you taste so good.)
So yummy, added Cranberries
Delicious, I loved it…I use pomegranate arils in lieu of apples, a nice change of pace
